findings.title: before_validation callback can crash on nil host
findings.body: `self.host.sub!(...)` will raise NoMethodError if `host` is nil (e.g. creating a record without host param). The controller sets host from params but doesn't guard against missing/blank input before calling save, so a malformed request to the admin controller could 500 instead of returning a validation error.

findings.title: No existence check for update/destroy
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil if the id doesn't exist, and `save_host(nil)` or `host.destroy` will then raise NoMethodError on nil, producing a 500 instead of a 404/error response.

findings.title: Host regex rejects hosts with port but description allows paths/ports loosely
findings.body: The validation regex requires a TLD segment of 2-5 chars, which will reject valid TLDs longer than 5 characters (e.g. .london, .company) and some edge-case valid hostnames, limiting legitimate host entries without an easy way to override.

findings.title: SQL injection risk in migration via string interpolation
findings.body: The migration builds raw SQL using string interpolation of untrusted site_setting values (`h`) without escaping/quoting: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. If an existing embeddable_hosts setting value contains a single quote or malicious SQL, this could break the migration or allow SQL injection during upgrade.

findings.title: Dropped explicit 'embeddable hosts not set' check changes behavior silently
findings.body: Previously there was an explicit error for blank embeddable_hosts setting; now that check is removed and only `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` is used. If no EmbeddableHost records exist, `host_allowed?` will simply return false, giving the same generic 'invalid referer host' error for both 'not configured' and 'wrong host' cases, which is less informative for admins debugging configuration issues.

findings.title: Fragile string replace for underscore model names
findings.body: `type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore occurrence, not all occurrences (no global flag). If a model type name contains multiple underscores, this basePath check would fail to properly normalize the type and could incorrectly treat it as a non-admin model or vice versa.
